thread: Subject: Re: Re: Invoice HL-20931 charged twice

I'm writing for the third time about invoice HL-20931. My card statement for October shows two charges of $249.00 from Harbourlight on the 3rd, a minute apart. Your reply last week said one of them was a pending authorisation that would drop off within five working days. It has now been nine working days and both charges have settled. I've attached a screenshot of the statement with my card number hidden.

I'd like one of the two charges refunded to the same card, and a corrected receipt showing a single payment. I'm happy with the subscription itself and I don't want it cancelled; this is only about the double charge. If the refund can't go back to the card, a credit on the account would be acceptable, but I'd prefer the card.

Could you also tell me why this happened? The checkout page timed out the first time I pressed Pay, so I pressed it again. If that's the cause, it might be worth a warning on the page so it doesn't happen to anyone else.

Thank you for getting in touch, and sorry for the worry. We can see one completed payment of $249.00 for invoice HL-20931 on 3 October. A second attempt at the same time appears in our payment system as an authorisation, which your bank should release within five working days. If it hasn't gone by then, please reply to this email and we'll look into it straight away.
I've been charged twice for my annual renewal (invoice HL-20931). Both charges are for $249.00 and were taken on 3 October. Please refund one of them.

Your Harbourlight subscription has been renewed. Plan: Harbourlight Studio, annual. Amount: $249.00, paid by card ending 0417. Invoice: HL-20931. Renewal date: 3 October. Next renewal: 3 October next year. Your plan includes five seats, 2 TB of shared storage, priority email support and the desktop and mobile apps. To change your plan, add seats or download past invoices, open Billing in your account settings. If you didn't expect this renewal, you can cancel within 14 days for a full refund from the same page.

A reminder that your Harbourlight Studio plan renews on 3 October for $249.00. Nothing needs doing if you'd like to keep it: we'll charge the card on file, ending 0417. If your card has changed, please update it before the renewal date so that your team's access isn't interrupted. You can also switch to monthly billing at $24.00 a month, or move to the Team plan if you need more than five seats. Questions about your bill? Reply to this email and our accounts team will help.

Harbourlight Ltd, 14 Quay Street, Bristol. You are receiving this email because you have an account with us. Our support hours are 8am to 6pm, Monday to Friday. For urgent issues with a live service outage, call the number on your account page. Please don't reply with card numbers or passwords: we will never ask for them by email.
message: Hi! It's Sam from number 12. Hope you're well and the new kitchen is coming along. I've got a slightly cheeky favour to ask: we're finally clearing the gutters on Saturday morning and our ladder has given up (one of the feet snapped). Would we be able to borrow your long ladder, the aluminium one? We'd only need it for a couple of hours, probably from about nine until eleven, and I'll bring it back the same day, cleaned off. If Saturday doesn't work, Sunday would be fine too. No worries at all if you'd rather not lend it out. Also, our cat has been sitting on your shed roof again; tell me if she's being a nuisance and I'll try to keep her in. While I'm asking favours, Jo wanted me to check whether you're still up for the street's bring-and-share lunch on the 19th; she's putting a list together of who's bringing what, and someone said you make a very good apple cake. And if you ever need anything doing that needs two pairs of hands, just knock, we're around most weekends. Thanks so much, Sam
report: Cellar works: final report, prepared for the owners of Kestrel House

Summary. The cellar under the east wing was damp, poorly lit and partly unusable. Between March and June the walls were treated, a drainage channel and sump pump were fitted, the electrics were replaced, and new shelving was installed. The cellar is now dry, and all of its floor area can be used for storage. The total cost of the works was $18,400, against a budget of $20,000.

Damp. A survey in February found moisture readings of 30 to 40 percent in the lower half of the north and east walls, caused by groundwater rather than leaking pipes. The walls were stripped back to the brick, treated with a cement-based waterproof coating, and given a breathable lime render above it. Readings taken in late June were under 12 percent everywhere. Damp works cost $9,600.

Drainage. A channel was cut into the floor along the north wall and runs to a sump in the north-east corner, where an automatic pump lifts water into the existing drain outside. The pump has a float switch and a battery backup that runs for about eight hours in a power cut, and an alarm sounds in the kitchen if the water level rises past the pump. The pump should be checked once a year, ideally before winter. Drainage cost $4,100.

Electrics. The old cable and the single bulb were removed. The cellar now has its own circuit with a residual current device, four LED ceiling lights on a switch at the top of the stairs, and three double sockets at waist height on the south wall, one of which powers the pump. The certificate of the works is filed with the house papers. Electrics cost $2,300.

Shelving. Galvanised steel shelving was fitted along the south and west walls, raised 15 centimetres off the floor so that it stays dry in the unlikely event of a flood. It holds up to 150 kilograms a shelf. Shelving cost $1,900.

Ventilation. With the walls sealed, the cellar needs air moving through it, or condensation will form in summer. A small extractor fan was fitted high on the east wall, wired to a humidistat that runs it whenever the relative humidity rises above 65 percent. The fan is quiet and uses about four watts while it runs. Its filter can be rinsed under a tap and should be cleaned every six months. The cost of the fan is included in the electrics.

Floor. The old floor was uneven brick laid straight onto earth. Where the drainage channel was cut, the bricks were lifted, a damp-proof membrane was laid, and the floor was relaid on a thin concrete bed with a gentle fall towards the channel. The rest of the floor was cleaned and sealed. Floor works were part of the drainage cost.

Timeline. Work started on 4 March and finished on 27 June, three weeks later than planned, because the treated walls took longer to dry in a wet April. The house stayed in use throughout, and the cellar door was kept locked whenever the contractor was away.

Remaining items. The oak door at the top of the stairs sticks in wet weather and should be eased by a joiner. The small window on the east wall could be replaced with a vented one to help air flow; this was quoted at $650 and is not included above. The contractor's guarantee on the damp works lasts ten years from 30 June.
